newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Telefonica to meet over Antena 3 deal.
newsitem.headline: EU, Telefonica to meet over Antena 3 deal.

text.p: European Commission competition officials will meet representatives of Telefonica de Espana in the next few days concerning the acquisition by the Spanish telecoms group of a stake in television channel Antena 3.
"There will be contacts shortly with representatives from Telefonica," Commission spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida told reporters.

On Monday, Telefonica effectively assumed control of the private television channel in defiance of the Commission, which last week warned it to get European Union approval before going ahead with its purchase.

Vale de Almeida said the Commission wanted to have a "clear idea of the scale and importance of the decisions taken before we issue any judgment on these decisions taken by Telefonica and how they comply with European law."

The acquisition had been challenged by CanalSatelite, a Spanish digital television platform backed by France's Canal Plus , in the latest round of a battle for control of Spain's fledgling pay-TV market.

Vale de Almeida said the Commission, which had asked Telefonica to respond to the complaints, had received information from Telefonica concerning Monday's decisions as well as its reaction to CanalSatelite's challenge.
"The Commission is studying and assessing the data passed on to us from Telefonica," Vale de Almeida said.

Antena 3 Television shareholders approved Telefonica's acquisition at an extraordinary meeting on Monday, where Telefonica secretary general Jose Mas Millet and three other Telefonica directors were appointed to its board.
Telefonica argues that its purchase of 25 percent of Antena 3 Television is a domestic, not European, competition issue. It said it had informed Spain's competition watchdog of its plans.
The deal does not fall under EU merger rules since the firms realise more than two-thirds of their turnover in Spain, it says.
But CanalSatelite argued in two recent complaints before the European Commission that Telefonica was abusing its dominant position in breach of the EU's founding treaty.
The Commission had not decided before the Antena 3 shareholders meeting whether there was a breach but warned Telefonica last week that any decisions taken there could be reversed.
